source_title: Mass Effect Petition Reaches Massive Milestone - GameRant
source_excerpt:
A petition calling on Electronic Arts to "save" Mass Effect has surpassed 100,000 signatures just days after its launch. The campaign's momentum highlights the pressure fans are placing on EA to secure a future for the franchise following news that Mass Effect developer BioWare is closing.
Before the cancellation, BioWare had spent years publicly discussing the next Mass Effect game and said in November 2025 that the project was still in development under a core team led by several veteran developers who worked on the highly lauded original trilogy. The endeavor officially ended no later than October 21, when EA announced that it was closing BioWare and canceling Mass Effect 5 as a result .
Mass Effect Petition Surpasses 120,000 Signatures
The resulting #SaveMassEffect Change.org petition , created on October 21, had surpassed 121,000 signatures by 11:00 a.m. ET on October 24. Its growth accelerated rapidly, with more than 29,000 signatures added on October 22 before the total tripled by the following day. The petition calls on EA to either resume development of Mass Effect 5 with adequate resources or seriously consider licensing the franchise to another studio willing to continue it. Commander Shepard voice actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer have both encouraged fans to sign the petition and otherwise make their voices heard in support of keeping Mass Effect alive.
Because the Mass Effect petition is entirely fan-driven, its rapid growth in no way indicates that EA is close to reconsidering its controversial decision. The publisher's October 21 announcement was framed as final, meaning any reversal prompted by fan pressure would likely require a response far greater than the low-six-digit signatures amassed so far. Still, the petition's continued growth following its initial surge strongly suggests that a substantial segment of the Mass Effect fandom remains actively engaged and willing to mobilize around the future of the franchise.

It Is Still Unclear What Exact Stage of Development Mass Effect 5 Was In Before Cancelation
Unofficial Reports and Leaks Cast Doubt on EA's 'Early-Development' Framing
While Mass Effect 5 was already formally confirmed to be in the works back in December 2020, EA was still describing the project as being in "early development" six years later. The publisher used that exact wording in the late October 2026 letter announcing BioWare's closure. Subsequent reports citing studio insiders cast doubt on how little progress had been made, particularly after what was reportedly intended to be the first Mass Effect 5 trailer leaked online on October 22. The two-minute promotional video was rendered entirely in-engine and featured a much older Liara, seemingly still operating as the Shadow Broker, alongside glimpses of a story with a strong sci-fi spy-thriller tone. Bloomberg's Jason Schreier testified to the authenticity of the leaked footage, describing the trailer as genuine in a Bluesky post .
A separate Mass Effect 5 story leak offered considerably more alleged details about what BioWare had been building since 2020. YouTuber Dantics, who says he participated in one of BioWare's private community feedback groups, claimed the game would have been set more than 600 years after the Reaper War and followed a new N7 protagonist navigating a galactic cold war in which the Geth had emerged as a major power. He also alleged that BioWare planned to reconcile the three Mass Effect 3 endings into a shared continuity.
